newsitem.title: UK: Reduction in Houston Ship Channel closures planned.
newsitem.headline: Reduction in Houston Ship Channel closures planned.

text.p: Houston maritime officials are expected to reveal next week new specifications aimed at reducing closures while work is undertaken on the Houston Ship Channel this summer, according to the Port of Houston Authority.
The authority said it is discussing proposals with the Texas Department of Transportation and other maritime officials to seek new private sector bids for work to remove the Baytown Tunnel.
A bid which it was feared could lead to 55 closures of the channel over 15 weeks from mid-July has been rejected.

Port of Houston Authority spokeswoman Caleen Burton-Allen said the meeting, at the end of this week, would consider conditions to reduce closures while work on the tunnel went ahead. She expected to know the outcome early next week.

"We are hoping to revise the specifications so we can go out and advertise for bids in July for a plan which does not require so many closures. We do not want to inconvenience our customers," she said.
Work on the vehicle tunnel under the channel, which has been replaced by a bridge, is now likely to go ahead in August or September to allow dredging operations next year, she added.

The tunnel needs to be partially or fully removed before the Houston Ship Channel's depth is increased to 45 feet, from 40 feet, and its width extended to 530 feet, from 400 feet. Dredging will be carried out by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
By law the lowest priced bid for the tunnel work has to be accepted, but the original bid was rejected on grounds it was too disruptive and that the specifications needed to be amended.
Tanker owners had previously expressed concerns at the possibility of delays to berthing.
